display: Ilha do Mel & Pontal do Paraná
tagline: Paraná's car-free island jewel — a quarter-million park visitors a year, a state-regulated boat crossing as the only way in, and a UNESCO-flanked bay begging for clean, quiet water transit.
summary: Ilha do Mel is the most-visited state park in Paraná, a car-free island at the mouth of Paranaguá Bay where every single visitor — 247,020 in 2025 — arrives by boat. The crossing from Pontal do Sul is a formally regulated public water-transport service with state-approved tariffs (AGEPAR), a daily visitor cap, and a brand-new R$9.9 million electronic ticketing and access-control system. Around it spreads one of Brazil's great protected estuaries: the heritage port city of Paranaguá, the fishing islands of Peças and Amparo, and Superagui National Park inside the UNESCO Atlantic Forest World Heritage area. Today all of it moves on slow diesel launches. A foiling-electric fleet turns the 30-minute barca into an 8-minute glide, collapses the 90-minute Paranaguá run to half an hour, and puts near-silent, zero-emission boats in waters where botos-cinza dolphins feed beside the piers.

demand_signals.label: Park visitation (2025)
demand_signals.value: 247,020 visitors — Paraná's most-visited state park, up 21% on 2024; 37,924 in December alone
demand_signals.note: Every visitor arrives by boat; the island is car-free
demand_signals.source: Instituto Água e Terra (IAT) 2025 park visitation release

demand_signals.label: Boat passengers embarked (2025)
demand_signals.value: 383,162 passengers boarded for the island in 2025
demand_signals.note: Count from Abaline, the boatmen's association that operates the official crossing
demand_signals.source: Abaline via Gazeta do Povo, Jan 2026

demand_signals.label: Regulated water-transit corridor
demand_signals.value: Pontal do Sul ↔ Ilha do Mel crossing is a state-regulated public service: AGEPAR-approved tariffs (R$44.77 regular / R$69.07 nautical taxi, round trip, 2023 adjustment), credentialed vessels, official public terminal
demand_signals.note: A rare LatAm case of a formally tariffed, regulator-supervised small-boat passenger corridor — an adopted daily habit to modernise, not demand to create
demand_signals.source: AGEPAR Resolução nº 010/2023; AGEPAR Travessias Marítimas — Ilha do Mel page

demand_signals.label: Access-control modernisation underway
demand_signals.value: Daily visitor cap of 5,000 rising to 11,000 under the island's new legal framework (Lei Estadual 22.315/2025); R$9.9M electronic ticketing + flow-management contract signed Dec 2025 (Consórcio Ilha do Mel / Imply)
demand_signals.note: The state is re-tooling how people board for the island right now — an open design-in window for a cleaner, faster fleet
demand_signals.source: Gazeta do Povo, 02 Jan 2026; Lei Estadual nº 22.315/2025

demand_signals.label: Protected-waters bay network
demand_signals.value: Superagui National Park (UNESCO Atlantic Forest World Heritage) plus Ilha das Peças, Amparo and Guaraqueçaba are all served by scheduled boats from Paranaguá today (R$20–90 per person)
demand_signals.note: 93% of Ilha do Mel itself is under conservation protection; the bay hosts resident botos-cinza dolphins — a concrete case for silent, zero-emission, low-wake vessels
demand_signals.source: Folha do Litoral, Feb 2025; IAT PEIM page

use_cases.title: The regulated crossing, electrified
use_cases.body: Replace the diesel barca queue on the official Pontal do Sul ↔ Nova Brasília / Encantadas crossing (~2–3 nm) with scheduled foiling shuttles — an 8-minute, near-silent glide slotting straight into the new electronic ticketing and access-cap system.

use_cases.title: Paranaguá heritage corridor
use_cases.body: From the historic Rua da Praia waterfront of Paranaguá — Brazil's second-oldest city and a working port — today's 1h30 launch to the island becomes a ~30-minute flight above the bay, opening the city's hotels, cruise calls and railway-tourist flow (the Serra do Mar train from Curitiba) to same-day island trips.

use_cases.title: UNESCO bay spider
use_cases.body: Small-group eco-charters from Ilha do Mel and Paranaguá across the Lagamar estuary — Superagui's deserted 38 km beach, Ilha das Peças' dolphin waters, Guaraqueçaba's fishing villages — silent and low-wake inside a national park and World Heritage area where diesel excursion boats run today.

use_cases.title: Inter-village island link
use_cases.body: Encantadas and Nova Brasília, the island's two villages and piers, are separated by a hilly 1.5–2 hour walking trail; a foiling water taxi makes it a minutes-long hop and lets day visitors see both ends of the island within the visitor-cap window.

journeys.to: Ilha do Mel — Nova Brasília trapiche
journeys.today: A 30-minute diesel barca, every 30–60 minutes, R$44.77 round trip at the regulated tariff — with summer queues at the terminal.
journeys.with_navier: An ~8-minute, near-silent foiling shuttle, no wake through the anchorage, timed to the island's electronic access-control slots.

journeys.today: A 1h30 launch across the bay (~R$80–90 per person, limited departures), or skip Paranaguá entirely and drive an extra hour to Pontal do Sul.
journeys.with_navier: A ~30-minute flight above the bay channel from the historic city centre, making the heritage port the island's natural gateway again.

journeys.today: A hilly 1.5–2 hour walking trail across the island, or an informal local boat transfer.
journeys.with_navier: A 5-minute foiling hop between the island's two piers — both villages in one day trip.

journeys.to: Superagui (Barra do Superagui, UNESCO national park)
journeys.today: One scheduled boat a day on weekdays (14:00, R$60), around three hours en route via the bay channels.
journeys.with_navier: Under an hour, silent and low-wake inside the World Heritage estuary — Superagui becomes a day trip instead of an expedition.

journeys.today: A ~50-minute nautical taxi across the northern bay, limited daily departures serving one of Brazil's most isolated municipal seats.
journeys.with_navier: A ~35-minute smooth foiling run — reliable, clean transit for a community whose road access is a notorious dirt track.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire mesh is short-range and sheltered: Pontal do Sul ↔ island piers (~2–3 nm), inter-village hop (~2 nm), Paranaguá ↔ island (~12 nm), and the Lagamar eco-spider to Ilha das Peças, Superagui and Guaraqueçaba (~11–19 nm) all sit far inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with charging at the Pontal do Sul public terminal and Paranaguá waterfront. Low-wake, near-silent operation matters here: 93% of Ilha do Mel is under conservation protection and resident dolphins feed through the bay.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: As the network grows, Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range links this bay south along the Paraná and Santa Catarina coast — Guaratuba, Itajaí/Balneário Camboriú and Florianópolis — and north toward the São Paulo coast (Cananéia and the Lagamar continue across the state line), with no charging-infrastructure dependency at the remote ends.

competitive_landscape: The water is run today by Abaline — the boatmen's association that has operated the official Ilha do Mel crossing for decades and holds the sole ticket concession — alongside SEIL-credentialed nautical taxis and Barcopar's tour boats out of Paranaguá. 383,162 passengers boarded in 2025 on conventional diesel launches: 30 minutes from Pontal do Sul, 1h30 from Paranaguá, one boat a day to Superagui. The demand is proven, regulated and growing (+21% park visitation in a year); the experience is slow, loud and diesel in waters that are almost entirely under conservation protection. There is no fast, clean incumbent — and the state is actively modernising terminals, ticketing and access control right now.
seasonality: Peak season runs December through Carnival (austral summer): Abaline raises crossing frequency, the island hits its daily visitor cap on holiday peaks, and afternoon thunderstorms pass through. April–November is a long, mild subtropical shoulder with steady weekend flow. The crossings and the whole bay mesh run in sheltered estuary water behind the island; only the island's ocean-facing beaches take Atlantic swell. Passing winter cold fronts bring wind chop to the bay — exactly the conditions foiling smooths out. No cyclone exposure.
regulatory_note: Unusually mature water-transit governance for a market this size: AGEPAR (the Paraná state regulator) approves crossing tariffs and monitors service quality (Resolutions 010/2023, 025/2023); SEIL credentials vessels via public calls (chamamento público 001/2019 regular, 01/2025 nautical taxi); the Pontal do Paraná municipality manages the public terminal and its embarkation fee; IAT manages the state park and the visitor cap under Lei Estadual 22.315/2025 (5,000/day today, up to 11,000 with the new electronic control); the Brazilian Navy's Capitania dos Portos governs vessel safety class and crew. The December 2025 access-control and ticketing contract makes this the moment to specify the next fleet generation.
signature_routes: Pontal do Sul ↔ Ilha do Mel / Nova Brasília (the regulated crossing, ~3 nm)
Paranaguá ↔ Ilha do Mel (heritage-port bay corridor, ~12 nm)

precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that electric foiling can be the backbone of an island transport system at national scale — the same pattern as a regulated island crossing, at larger scale.
